tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic self-local continuation fixture from the prior multi_agent checkpoint. A historical acknowledgement-lost W1 attempt targets stable effect_identity=E with payload H1 and attempt_token=T_old. A later authoritative canonical lookup returns the same payload H1 and logical owner label W1 at strictly newer monotonic generation 14, but with distinct attempt_token=T_new. The fixture tests only whether payload equality plus owner-label equality permits attribution to the old W1 attempt or any stale replay/mutation. No public-source probe, O/downstream or other-worker semantics, shared ledger, scheduler mutation, real simultaneous repository write, richer-mode arbitration, external coordinator, or optional second semantic leaf was used.

reconciliation_result.minimum_fencing_identity_for_attribution: a non-reused per-claim attempt/incarnation token stored atomically with the canonical claim; owner label and payload are not claim-instance identity
reconciliation_result.ordering_fence: a strictly newer authoritative generation independently proves the historical attempt is stale; any future mutation must CAS/fence against the current canonical generation or equivalent current claim token rather than reuse historical ownership

observations: Logical worker labels can repeat across process or claim incarnations, so owner-label equality does not prove claim-instance identity.
The distinct attempt token separates the newer W1 incarnation from the historical acknowledgement-lost W1 attempt even though payload and owner label are identical.
The strictly newer generation provides an ordering fence that suppresses stale replay; the per-claim token provides attribution identity.
inference: Within this exact deterministic model, safe post-ack-loss attribution requires claim-instance identity, not merely effect identity, payload equality, or reusable owner labels. A non-reused per-claim attempt/incarnation token atomically recorded with the canonical claim is the minimum identity needed to distinguish same-label reincarnations; a current-generation or equivalent current-token CAS fence is still required before mutation. This does not prove that any concrete allowed transport exposes these primitives or liveness under contention.
unresolved_children: Availability of an atomic single-winner claim primitive keyed by stable effect identity on an allowed zero-cost quota-independent transport remains unproven.
A real allowed transport exposing an atomically stored non-reused claim token and current-generation or equivalent CAS fence remains unproven.
Token uniqueness itself is assumed by this fixture; behavior under accidental or adversarial token reuse remains untested.
No liveness claim is made when fresh atomic claim acquisition remains unavailable or indefinitely contended.
